analysis.title: GS Pasquariello - markets / macro 18 Oct 2026
key_insights: Goldman's Pasquariello says the AI trade has entered a more complicated phase for both credit and equity markets. The shift in narrative challenged consensus positions and triggered significant risk reduction.

US equities fell sharply in the week to 16 Oct. NDX went 0-5 and the S&P dropped 2%, losing the escape velocity from its early-October breakout from a multi-month consolidation. Pasquariello's long stocks / short bonds pairing also lost money.
Possible catalysts for the week's selloff: the CPI data, higher highs in deferred Brent contracts, and strong earnings (ASML, TSMC) not being rewarded.

The AI narrative debate now centers on both the availability and the cost of capital. GS's AI credit spread basket (GSUCHS30) gapped to the wides of the year. The AI leaders-vs-laggards basket was up nearly 100% YTD at end of June and has given back all of that performance since.

The gap between perceived high-quality and low-quality assets is widening. HY is underperforming IG in credit, and the GS high quality vs low quality pair trade (GSP1QUAL) rose sharply over the past month.
The GS hedge fund VIP pair trade (GSTHVIPP) had its worst week since the depths of COVID.

Since the Iran war broke out, the central market tension has been strong earnings growth against headwinds from energy and interest rates. Recently the market has struggled because of a gathering consensus that large upward estimate revisions are likely behind us, and because higher rates came into play.

For the first time in three years, several asset markets (high-velocity stocks, high yield credit, certain sovereign bond markets) felt the 'speed limit' from the bond market. The backup in rates was arrested late in the week. The last discrete comparable was SVB in early 2023, or NDX in late 2023 in a broad sense.

Cyclicals continue to struggle. RTY broke down through its 200-day moving average and BKX did the same despite fine Q3 earnings. CAT, VRT and GEV charts are cited as examples. The open question is whether the downgrade of the growth outlook has gone far enough.

Flows were decisively risk-off. GS saw several waves of supply from long-only and hedge fund clients. Tech had the largest week of net selling in at least a decade, skewed to semis. Recent weeks saw the largest supply of global AI stocks since the launch of ChatGPT, taking exposure to the 35th percentile of the past year.

Options markets showed anxiety. VIX rose to 20 (+5 points w/w), the front of the VIX futures curve is inverted, VIX call volume was very significant and S&P put notional traded was a record. Pasquariello says the market is cleaner than it was a few weeks ago.

Pasquariello expects a few more pockets of supply toward month-end (mutual fund fiscal year-end, risk reduction ahead of the midterms). After that, corporate repurchases should become the dominant technical. November is the second-largest month of the year for buybacks.

The key fundamental question is whether Q3 earnings can restore confidence. The first pressure test is META on Wednesday. Pasquariello is still inclined to think September/October choppiness gives way to strength in November and December.

sector_views.rationale: Record net selling in tech, skewed to semis, took AI stock exposure to the 35th percentile of the past year. The AI leaders basket gave back all of its YTD gain.
RTY and BKX broke through their 200-day moving averages. Higher energy costs and interest rates are weighing on cyclicals, including CAT, VRT and GEV.

earnings_insights: Q3 earnings season is underway. Pasquariello calls the Q3 earnings for banks (BKX) 'totally fine' yet BKX still broke down through its 200-day moving average.
ASML and TSMC reported strong earnings that were not rewarded by the market.
META reports Wednesday and is the first pressure test of whether Q3 earnings can restore confidence.
There is a gathering consensus that the recent trend of large upward revisions to analyst estimates is likely behind us.

macro_indicators.reading: Not quantified in the report. Named as one possible catalyst for the week's selloff.
macro_indicators.interpretation: The CPI data is one of the cited catalysts for the risk-off week and the backup in US rates.
Higher energy costs compound with higher interest rates to weigh on the growth outlook and cyclicals.

risk_factors: Further position reduction toward month-end (mutual fund fiscal year-end, pre-midterm de-risking).
Higher US rates and energy prices continue to constrain high-velocity stocks, high yield credit and some sovereign bond markets.
Q3 earnings fail to restore confidence, with the market not rewarding strong results.
Further widening of AI credit spreads and the cost and availability of capital for AI.
Estimate revisions have peaked, removing a prior support for equities.
vol_and_positioning: VIX rose to 20, up 5 full points w/w.
The front end of the VIX futures curve is inverted.
Very significant volume in VIX calls and record notional traded in S&P puts.
Tech had its largest week of net selling in at least a decade, skewed to semis, from both long-only and hedge funds across fundamental, systematic and diversified types.
Global AI stock exposure fell to the 35th percentile of the past year after the largest patch of supply since the launch of ChatGPT.
The GS hedge fund VIP pair trade (GSTHVIPP) had its worst week since the depths of COVID.

Pasquariello expects more supply pockets toward month-end (mutual fund fiscal year-end, pre-midterm risk reduction), then corporate buybacks as the dominant technical. November is the second-largest month for buybacks.
geopolitical: The Iran war: since it broke out, the market's central tension has been strong earnings growth against headwinds from energy and interest rates.
US midterms: risk reduction ahead of the midterms is expected to add supply late in the month.

tension_points.theme: Q3 earnings vs rates and energy
tension_points.bull_case: Earnings have been the north star for the market for four years and buoyed it in the Q1 and Q2 reporting periods. Buybacks should become the dominant technical after month-end, and Pasquariello leans toward strength in November and December.
tension_points.bear_case: Large upward estimate revisions are likely behind us. Higher energy costs and interest rates are weighing on cyclicals and high-velocity stocks, and strong earnings from ASML and TSMC were not rewarded.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q3 earnings, starting with META on Wednesday, failing to restore confidence.
